intent: Eight individual tasks distinguish changed views, relevant two-person dialogue, three agreed actions, speech openings, listening instructions, future announcements, news timing and newspaper material use.

transfer.stem: Which summary keeps the exchange, action count and announcement?
transfer.passage:
Preparing our club communication
A conversation changed my view of a problem, but that did not mean the problem was solved. For a separate writing task, we chose a short exchange between two travellers: “Is this seat free?” “Yes, you can sit here.” The reply answered the question; two unrelated remarks would not do the same job. The picture supplied a setting, not proof of an actual conversation.
Our discussion ended with three clear actions. In the exercise, one card represented one action, so we needed three cards. That did not add action details or prove that the actions had been carried out. A pupil opened her speech with a surprising question. We knew where the question came in the speech, but not its wording or answer.
At the station, we were told to listen carefully to an announcement. No announcement text or recording was supplied in this task, so we could not infer a train number or time. The winners would be announced after lunch; their names were not given, and the announcement had not been reported as complete.
Good news reached us before dinner, although this account did not state its content. Finally, we read an instruction about wrapping broken glass in old newspaper. It used newspaper as wrapping material; the task only checked the sentence meaning and did not ask us to handle glass.

options.text: The travellers exchanged unrelated remarks; three actions meant three exercise cards; the winners would be announced after lunch.
One traveller answered the other; three actions meant all had already been done; the winners would be announced after lunch.
One traveller answered the other; three actions meant three exercise cards; the winners would be announced after lunch.
One traveller answered the other; three actions meant three exercise cards; the winners had already been announced before lunch.
